package_info.why_malicious: These packages are backdoored clones of legitimate npm packages (passport, bcryptjs, etherscan-api) and contain obfuscated JavaScript code that implements the BeaverTail infostealer and downloader malware. The malware exfiltrates sensitive data (cryptocurrency wallets, browser caches, login keychains) to attacker-controlled C2 servers and downloads a second-stage Python backdoor (InvisibleFerret). The only difference from the legitimate packages is the presence of a single, highly obfuscated malicious line, indicating intentional supply chain compromise.

execution_context.file_location: main source file of passports-js and bcrypts-js (obfuscated line inserted among unobfuscated code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects browser extension data, cryptocurrency wallet information, and keychain data, then exfiltrates this data to http://95.164.17.24:1224/uploads via HTTP POST, and downloads a second-stage Python backdoor from http://95.164.17.24:1224/client/3/726 for execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is highly obfuscated and executes immediately upon import, performing credential and wallet data theft and network exfiltration, which are classic infostealer behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate authentication or cryptography libraries should not access browser caches, keychains, or perform network exfiltration on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software updaters or telemetry modules may contact remote servers, but not for credential or wallet data exfiltration.
key_indicators: Obfuscated single-line JavaScript in an otherwise unobfuscated file
Immediate data collection and exfiltration to hardcoded C2
Download and execution of a remote Python payload

execution_context.file_location: dedicated source file in blockscan-api (obfuscated line as sole file content)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects browser extension data, cryptocurrency wallet information, and keychain data, then exfiltrates this data to http://95.164.17.24:1224/uploads via HTTP POST, and downloads a second-stage Python backdoor from http://95.164.17.24:1224/client/3/525 for execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and executes immediately, targeting sensitive user data and communicating with a known malicious C2 server. The campaign ID in the URL indicates targeted attack segmentation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A package providing Etherscan API access should not access browser or keychain data, nor download and execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate API wrappers do not require this behavior.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code as the only content in a source file
Hardcoded C2 infrastructure and campaign ID

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious npm package (passports-js, bcrypts-js, or blockscan-api).
Malicious code collects sensitive data (browser extension info, cryptocurrency wallets, keychains).
Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled C2 server at http://95.164.17.24:1224/uploads.
Malware downloads and executes a second-stage Python backdoor (InvisibleFerret) from http://95.164.17.24:1224/client/3/<campaign ID>.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent remote access to the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript code executing at import-time
Immediate network connections to hardcoded IPs/domains on import
Access to browser extension directories, keychains, or wallet files by non-browser packages
Download and execution of remote Python payloads from suspicious URLs
file_indicators: Single long obfuscated line in an otherwise unobfuscated JavaScript file
Obfuscated code as the only content in a source file
Unexpected network or filesystem access in packages named similarly to popular libraries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with obfuscated JavaScript code that executes at import-time, especially if the code makes network requests to hardcoded IP addresses or exfiltrates data to suspicious endpoints. Flag packages that access browser extension directories, keychains, or cryptocurrency wallet files outside of expected contexts. Use static analysis to detect single-line obfuscated code in packages with names similar to popular libraries. Network monitoring should alert on connections to 95.164.17.24:1224 and related URL paths.
